result.title: S$^2$LMR: Supervised Sequential Long-Context Multi-Step Retriever
result.summary: Multi-step retrieval over long contexts is a key capability for retrieval-augmented generation, but strong existing approaches are costly and complex to train. Supervised retrievers are far simpler and cheaper, yet they fall well behind in this setting. We show that this gap stems not from supervised training itself, but from three misalignments between training and inference: easy training negatives, noisy retrieval prefixes, and position-agnostic scoring. Guided by this analysis, we introduce S$^2$LMR, a simple yet effective supervised sequential retriever that models multi-step retrieval as the evolution of an explicit textual state encoded by a single shared Transformer. On long-context reasoning, multi-hop QA, and needle-in-a-haystack benchmarks with context lengths ranging from 4K to 10M tokens, S$^2$LMR achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods, substantially outperforming prior supervised retrievers. Notably, it requires only $\sim$2 hours of training on a single A6000 for contexts of up to 10M tokens, while remaining robust across a wide range of hyperparameter settings.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将长上下文多步检索建模为显式文本状态的逐步演化，由单个共享 Transformer 编码，并指出监督式检索器落后的原因在于训练/推理的三处错配（简单负样本、含噪检索前缀、与位置无关的打分），据此给出简洁高效的监督方案。
AI.relevance_reason: 其显式文本状态演化可作为 latent 推理状态的对照基线，训练-推理错配分析（尤其含噪前缀与位置无关打分）可能为 LVR 的轨迹训练、证据累积与位置敏感的 latent 状态评价提供可核查线索。
